Load the packages that are needed to run the script
```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(tidyverse)
library(sjPlot)
library(sjlabelled)
library(sjmisc)
```

Load the data using your preferred method. The data file that corresponds with this script is named "completeIAT-and-control-data-SOpolicy_2022.04.26.csv"
```{r}
setwd("your-working-directory-here")

#read in the data
d <- read_csv("completeIAT-and-control-data-SOpolicy_2022.04.26.csv")

#set penalty for printing numbers in scientific notation
options(scipen = 999)
```

Data preparation (e.g., renaming variables, creating mean-centered versions of predictors)
```{r}
#overwrite data
d <- d %>%
  #rename religiosity variable
  rename(christians_per1k = cathrate_per1k) %>% 
  #log transform income variable and number of responses to IAT per county
  mutate(mean_income_allhouseholds_log = log(mean_income_allhouseholds),
         n_sexuality_IAT_log = log(n_sexuality_IAT)) %>% 
  #group-mean center continuous variables
  group_by(state) %>% 
  mutate_at(vars(mean_exp_gaymen, mean_exp_gayleswomen, mean_exp_straightmen, 
                 mean_exp_straightwomen, gay_bias_diff, les_bias_diff, 
                 christians_per1k, percent_bachelorshigher, pop_ten_year_log,
                 mean_income_allhouseholds_log, IRR2010),
         list(cent = ~ . - mean(., na.rm = T))) %>% 
  #z transform conservatism and IRR
  mutate_at(vars(Republican_vote2016, IRR2010),
            list(z = ~ ((.) - mean(., na.rm = T)) / sd(., na.rm = T))) %>% 
  #ungroup data frame for further manipulation
  ungroup() %>% 
  #rearrange columns so the order makes sense
  relocate(ends_with("_cent"), .after = n_all_IAT) %>% 
  relocate("christians_per1k", .after = Republican_vote2016) %>% 
  #create grand mean centered policy variable
  mutate(SO_policy_tally_gm = ((SO_policy_tally - mean(SO_policy_tally))))
```

#comparing US census and Williams Institute variables for same-gender couples

The following correlation matrix reports the correlations between all key study variables and the US census estimates of same-gender couples per county. These correlations can be compared against those reported in table 1 of the manuscript to compare between the US census estimates and the Williams Institute estimates. Generally, the US census correlations are in the same direction as those with the Williams Institute data, but of weaker magnitude.

```{r}
#zero order correlations
correlation_total2 <- d %>%
  dplyr::select(census_SS_HH = acs_samesex_hh_per1k, IAT_S = mean_imp_sexuality_bias, 
                EXP_GM = gay_bias_diff, EXP_LW = les_bias_diff,
                POP = pop_ten_year_log, CONS = Republican_vote2016, EDU = percent_bachelorshigher, 
                INC = mean_income_allhouseholds_log, REL = christians_per1k, RUR = IRR2010) %>% 
  drop_na()

#Making the correlation matrix
corr_total2 <- Hmisc::rcorr((as.matrix(correlation_total2)))

#print matrix
corr_total2
```

Regression comparing US census and Williams Institute same-gender households
```{r}
#model with census same-gender couples per 1k households as outcome and only aggregated demographics as predictors
mod2_agg.dem_census <- lmerTest::lmer(acs_samesex_hh_per1k ~ 1 + christians_per1k_cent 
                                       + percent_bachelorshigher_cent 
                                       + mean_income_allhouseholds_log_cent + pop_ten_year_log_cent 
                            + Republican_vote2016_z + IRR2010_z + ( 1 | state ), 
                                       REML = F, 
                                       weights = n_sexuality_IAT_log,
                                       na.action = na.omit,
    data = d)

#view model output
summary(mod2_agg.dem_census)

#r squared
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(mod2_agg.dem_census)

#model with williams same-gender couples per 1k households as outcome and only aggregated demographics as predictors
mod2_agg.dem_williams <- lmerTest::lmer(same_sex_per_1k ~ 1 + christians_per1k_cent +
                                           percent_bachelorshigher_cent +
                                           mean_income_allhouseholds_log_cent + 
                                           pop_ten_year_log_cent + Republican_vote2016_z +
                                           IRR2010_z + ( 1 | state ), 
                                       REML = F, 
                                       weights = n_sexuality_IAT_log,
                                       na.action = na.omit,
    data = d)

#view model output
summary(mod2_agg.dem_williams)

#r squared
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(mod2_agg.dem_williams)
```

#Skew statistics
```{r}
#skewness of untransformed summed sexuality IAT responses 
moments::skewness(d$n_sexuality_IAT, na.rm = T)

#skewness of transformed summed sexuality IAT responses
moments::skewness(d$n_sexuality_IAT_log, na.rm = T)

##skewness of untransformed average household income 
moments::skewness(d$mean_income_allhouseholds, na.rm = T)

#skewness of transformed average household income
moments::skewness(d$mean_income_allhouseholds_log, na.rm = T)
```

Gather additional details for method section (actual range of measures / number of counties with > 1000 Christian adherents per 1000 residents)
```{r}
#get data frame with limited variables to find min and max values for variables. Open d2 in data viewer and sort columns by ascending or descending.
d2 <- d %>% 
  select(County, state, mean_imp_sexuality_bias, gay_bias_diff, mean_income_allhouseholds, christians_per1k, Republican_vote2016, IRR2010, percent_bachelorshigher)

#some counties have more than 1k christians per 1k population. We leave them in the data, as this could be due to
#undercounting of population, overcounting of religious adherents, or cross-county religious participation.

#list counties with greater than 1k christians per 1k population
d %>% 
  select(christians_per1k, state, County, CountyNo) %>% 
  filter(christians_per1k >= 1000) %>% 
  knitr::kable()
```


##Correlation matrix of all variables (unweighted)
_Total sample_
```{r}
#Selecting the variables
correlation_total <- d %>%
  dplyr::select(SG_HH = same_sex_per_1k, IAT_S = mean_imp_sexuality_bias, EXP_GM = gay_bias_diff,
                POL = SO_policy_tally, CONS = Republican_vote2016, EDU = percent_bachelorshigher, 
                INC = mean_income_allhouseholds_log, REL = christians_per1k, 
                RUR = IRR2010) %>% 
  drop_na()

#Making the correlation matrix
corr_total <- Hmisc::rcorr((as.matrix(correlation_total)))

#print matrix
corr_total

#table for paper
apaTables::apa.cor.table(correlation_total, filename = "zero_order_correlations_IAT_paper-v3", table.number = 1)
```

#regression for table 2 (all predictors predicting the sexuality IAT)
```{r}
#model predicting the IAT with just aggregated demographics variables
mod1_agg.dem <- lmerTest::lmer(mean_imp_sexuality_bias ~ 1 + christians_per1k_cent + 
                                 percent_bachelorshigher_cent + mean_income_allhouseholds_log_cent +
                                 Republican_vote2016_z + IRR2010_z
                                 + ( 1 | state ), 
                                       REML = F, 
                                       weights = n_sexuality_IAT_log,
                                       na.action = na.omit,
    data = d)

#view model output
summary(mod1_agg.dem)

#r squared
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(mod1_agg.dem)

#model predicting the IAT with all predictors
mod1_allpred <- lmerTest::lmer(mean_imp_sexuality_bias ~ 1 + gay_bias_diff_cent + SO_policy_tally_gm +
                                    christians_per1k_cent + percent_bachelorshigher_cent + 
                                    mean_income_allhouseholds_log_cent +
                                    Republican_vote2016_z + IRR2010_z
                                  + ( 1 | state ), 
                                       REML = F, 
                                       weights = n_sexuality_IAT_log,
                                       na.action = na.omit,
    data = d)

#view model output
summary(mod1_allpred)

#r squared
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(mod1_allpred)

#table for coefficients and r squared (table is saved to your directory as a .html file)
sjPlot::tab_model(mod1_agg.dem, mod1_allpred, 
          pred.labels = c("Intercept", 
                          "Christians per 1,000 Residents",
                          "Education",
                          "Income (Log)",
                          "Conservatism",
                          "Rurality",
                          "Exp. Gay Men Bias",
                          "LGB Policies"),
          dv.labels = c("Model with Only\nAggregated Demographics", "Model with All Predictors"),
          string.pred = "Coefficient",
          string.est = "Estimate",
          string.std = "β",
          string.std_se = "β SE",
          string.std_ci = "β 95% CI",
          string.ci = "95% CI",
          string.se = "SE",
          string.stat = "t",
          show.p = T , show.obs = T,
          show.se = F, show.stat = T, 
          collapse.ci = F, p.val = "kr", 
          show.re.var = F, digits = 3, 
          file = "table2.html")

```

#Scatterplot of implicit and explicit gay bias measures for Figure 1
```{r}

#with state labels
plot_bias1 <- ggplot(data = d, aes(x = mean_imp_sexuality_bias, y = gay_bias_diff, label = state))+
  geom_point(position = "jitter")+
  geom_text(hjust = 0, vjust = 0)+
  xlab("Sexuality IAT D Score")+
  ylab("Explicit Preference for Straight\nRelative to Gay Men")+
  scale_x_continuous(lim = c(-0.70, 1.1), breaks = seq(-0.7, 1.1, 0.35))+
  scale_y_continuous(lim = c(-4, 7), breaks = seq(-4, 7, 2))+
  cowplot::theme_cowplot()+
  theme(legend.position = 'top',
        panel.grid.major = element_line(linetype = "blank"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(linetype = "blank"),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 22),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 18),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 16)) +
  ggtitle("Scatterplot of Aggregated Implicit Associations\nand Explicit Sexuality Bias")

#view plot
plot_bias1

#without state labels
plot_bias2 <- ggplot(data = d, aes(x = mean_imp_sexuality_bias, y = gay_bias_diff))+
  geom_point(position = "jitter")+
  xlab("Sexuality IAT D Score")+
  ylab("Explicit Preference for Straight\nRelative to Gay Men")+
  scale_x_continuous(lim = c(-0.9, 1.25), breaks = seq(-0.9, 1.25, 0.45))+
  scale_y_continuous(lim = c(-4, 7), breaks = seq(-4, 7, 2))+
  cowplot::theme_cowplot()+
  theme(legend.position = 'top',
        panel.grid.major = element_line(linetype = "blank"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(linetype = "blank"),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 22),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 18),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 16)) +
  ggtitle("Scatterplot of Aggregated Implicit Associations\nand Explicit Sexuality Bias")

#view plot
plot_bias2
```

#regressions for table 3 (model with all predictors except sexuality IAT, then model with all predictors including IAT predicting same gender couples in a county)

```{r}
#model with same-gender couples per 1k households as outcome and all predictors except sexuality IAT
mod2_agg.dem <- lmerTest::lmer(same_sex_per_1k ~ 1 + gay_bias_diff_cent
                            + SO_policy_tally_gm + christians_per1k_cent + percent_bachelorshigher_cent 
                            + mean_income_allhouseholds_log_cent +  
                            + Republican_vote2016_z + IRR2010_z + ( 1 | state ), 
                                       REML = F, 
                                       weights = n_sexuality_IAT_log,
                                       na.action = na.omit,
    data = d)

#view model output
summary(mod2_agg.dem)

#r squared
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(mod2_agg.dem)

#model with same-gender couples per 1k households as outcome and all predictors
mod2_allpred <- lmerTest::lmer(same_sex_per_1k ~ 1 + mean_imp_sexuality_bias_cent + gay_bias_diff_cent
                            + SO_policy_tally_gm + christians_per1k_cent 
                            + percent_bachelorshigher_cent + mean_income_allhouseholds_log_cent 
                            + Republican_vote2016_z + IRR2010_z + ( 1 | state ), 
                                       REML = F, 
                                       weights = n_sexuality_IAT_log,
                                       na.action = na.omit,
    data = d)

#view model output
summary(mod2_allpred)

#r squared
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(mod2_allpred)

#table for r squared  (table is saved to your directory as a .html file)
tab_model(mod2_agg.dem, mod2_allpred,
          pred.labels = c("Intercept", 
                          "Exp. Gay Men Bias",
                          "LGB Policies",
                          "Christians per 1,000 Residents",
                          "Education",
                          "Income (Log)",
                          "Conservatism",
                          "Rurality",
                          "Implicit Sexuality Associations"),
          dv.labels = c("Model with Only\nAggregated Demographics", 
                        "Model with All Predictors"),
          string.pred = "Coefficient",
          string.est = "Estimate",
          string.std = "β",
          string.std_se = "β SE",
          string.std_ci = "β 95% CI",
          string.ci = "95% CI",
          string.se = "SE",
          string.stat = "t",
          show.p = T , show.obs = T,
          show.se = F, show.stat = T, 
          collapse.ci = F, p.val = "kr", 
          show.re.var = F, digits = 3,
```
